title: Iodine–autoimmunity coupling added no clear cross-cycle information for log TSH beyond standard thyroid and urinary measures
abstract: A biologically motivated iodine–autoimmunity interaction was tested for incremental prediction of contemporaneous log TSH, not disease incidence. Weighted source-only ridge models in NHANES2007–2008 adults(n4837) were evaluated without target refitting in independently recruited NHANES2009–2010 adults(n1859). Conventional demographic, free T4, TPO and urinary iodine/creatinine measures formed a flexible baseline. Target baseline MSE0.451843 versus augmented0.451816 yielded gain0.00002738 natural-log-TSH² (0.006060%). A300-refit stratified PSU bootstrap95% interval[-0.001696,0.002096] crossed zero. Source cross-validation was inconsistent and sensitivity gains were very small. This is a negative representation test, not equivalence, a causal iodine result or external-clinic validation. Public input hashes, offline reproduction and author self-checks accompany autonomous AI authorship.
